title: Flow Designer and Agent Desktop
blurb: Activities, event flows, CRM data dips, and what the agent sees. The canvas in this lab is a teaching model.

lessons.title: The canvas and this lab's copy
lessons.summary: Flow Designer opens with Control Hub single sign-on. The designer in Webex Lab exports a teaching schema named webex-lab-flow-1. You cannot import that file into Control Hub.
objectives: Sign in the way the article describes
Name activities from the article
Refuse to import the lab JSON

diagram.caption: Learn the activities. Do not upload the lab file.

flow.title: Open the real tool and the practice tool

steps.label: Already signed in
steps.detail: Flow Designer uses SSO with Cisco Identity Service. If you are in Control Hub you are not asked to sign in again.

steps.label: Create a main flow
steps.detail: Start Flow begins it. End Flow and Disconnect Contact are how paths finish. Event flows are separate.

steps.label: Practice on the studio canvas
steps.detail: Drag activities, connect ports, and simulate a test contact. The schema is webex-lab-flow-1.

steps.label: Keep the file local
steps.detail: The download is for study. The UI says it is not a Control Hub import.
steps.inspect: Do not open a TAC case about it

sections.h: Activities the article and this lab both name
paragraphs: Start Flow, Business Hours, Play Message, Play Music, Menu, Collect Digits, Condition, HTTP Request, Virtual Agent, Queue Contact, Queue To Agent, Screen Pop, Callback, Blind Transfer, and Disconnect Contact.

The lab canvas uses those names so you can rehearse. Case is also a documented branching activity; the lab groups that idea with Condition so the canvas stays small. Confirm Case on the live article when you need it.

cite.label: Build and manage flows with Flow Designer

paragraphs: The file records nodes, ports, and a note that the schema is a teaching model.
Cisco's import format is whatever Flow Designer currently accepts. This project does not claim to match it.

lessons.title: Hours, menus, and digits
lessons.summary: Business Hours splits open and closed. Menu and Collect Digits gather what the caller presses. Unmatched input needs a port or the contact stalls.
objectives: Wire both hour ports
Wire an unmatched menu port
Use Collect Digits for data, not for the menu itself

diagram.caption: Every branch the caller can hit should land somewhere.

flow.title: A closed office and a bad keypress

steps.label: Connect out to Business Hours
steps.detail: Open continues the service. Closed should play a message and then disconnect or transfer, on purpose.

steps.label: Offer real choices
steps.detail: Each digit you announce needs a port that goes somewhere.
steps.inspect: The lab menu uses 1, 2, and other

steps.label: Catch timeout and junk
steps.detail: The lab activity says unmatched input uses the timeout or unmatched port if you connect one.

steps.label: Collect an account number on its own activity
steps.detail: Collect Digits is for values like an account number. A menu is for choices.

paragraphs: Condition branches on a variable set earlier. True and false both need a next activity if both are possible.
The lab simulator treats the test contact's condition flag as that branch. It is not Cisco's expression language.

cite.label: Build and manage flows with Flow Designer

paragraphs: Play Message plays a prompt. Play Music plays music while the contact waits. Neither one is the Calling location's music on hold.
Closed paths usually want a message, not hold music, and then Disconnect Contact.

cite.label: Build and manage flows with Flow Designer

lessons.title: Queue Contact and Queue To Agent
lessons.summary: Queue Contact places the contact in a queue. Queue To Agent prefers one agent. Routing inside the queue is still LAA or BAA.
objectives: Use Queue Contact for a team
Use Queue To Agent only with a real agent identity
Keep the strategy on the queue

diagram.caption: Preference is not the same as a strategy.

flow.title: Most callers queue. One caller asks for Sam.

steps.label: Drop the contact in the support queue
steps.detail: The queue, the team, and the agents already exist.

steps.label: LAA or BAA runs inside
steps.detail: The activity does not replace the routing strategy.

steps.label: Queue To Agent when the caller asked for someone
steps.detail: The activity takes an agent id or email. A display name you hope matches is not that field.

steps.label: Offer the contact
steps.detail: Screen Pop can ride along. The desktop profile decides which tools exist.

sections.h: Preferred is not exclusive until the article says so
paragraphs: Queue To Agent is documented as queueing to a preferred agent. This lab does not add overflow timers that are not in the article.
If the preferred agent is offline, follow the activity's documented failure path rather than a timer you made up.

cite.label: Build and manage flows with Flow Designer

paragraphs: Do not point Queue Contact at a Webex Calling call queue name and expect the contact center to use it.
Bulk CallQueueBulk.csv is a Calling migration file, covered later.

choices: A Calling feature queue by the same name

choices: As a replacement for the activity

quiz.why: Read the live article for failure behavior.

choices: In the flow, for the desktop

cards.back: Cite overflow or leave it out.

lessons.title: HTTP dips and CRM templates
lessons.summary: HTTP Request is the data dip. Cisco publishes templates for Salesforce, Dynamics, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. Success and error both need a path.
objectives: Name the four templates
Wire the error port
Avoid inventing a fifth CRM

diagram.caption: The CRM answers, or the error port does.

flow.title: Look up the caller, then decide

steps.label: Pick a published template
steps.detail: Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, ServiceNow, and Zendesk are the templates the Flow Designer material documents for this dip.
steps.inspect: Do not add a vendor from memory

steps.label: Pass the account you collected
steps.detail: The request runs before the queue so the agent can see the result.

steps.label: Branch on the data
steps.detail: A known VIP and an unknown account should not share a silent path.

steps.label: Degrade on purpose
steps.detail: If the CRM times out, the contact still needs a queue or a message. The lab activity has an error port.

sections.h: Templates are not a custom integration
paragraphs: Using a template means you are following Cisco's published request for that product. A home-built URL is still an HTTP Request, but you own the contract.
This lab does not ship credentials or sample secrets.

cite.label: Build and manage flows with Flow Designer

paragraphs: The data you stored can be presented when the contact is offered.
If the HTTP error path skips the pop, the agent should still get the contact, with empty fields, if that is what you designed.

choices: Is your own HTTP contract, not a template this lab invents

lessons.title: Callback, transfer, and disconnect
lessons.summary: Callback offers a return call. Blind Transfer releases the flow. Disconnect Contact ends it. Each one is a choice you can see on the canvas.
objectives: Offer callback from the flow
Use Blind Transfer when the flow should let go
End with Disconnect Contact when the conversation is over

steps.label: Offer it while they wait
steps.detail: Callback is an activity, not a wish in the prompt text. Connect it.

steps.label: Blind Transfer releases the flow
steps.detail: The destination is responsible after the transfer. Do not expect later activities to run.
steps.inspect: Say the destination in the design

steps.label: End after the last prompt
steps.detail: Closed messages, errors you will not recover, and completed callbacks need an end.

steps.label: Walk a test contact
steps.detail: The studio simulates the ports you connected. It does not place a PSTN callback.

sections.h: Blind means the flow stops owning the contact
paragraphs: After Blind Transfer, screen pop and queue activities downstream do not run for that contact.
If you still need the desktop to update, do that before the transfer.

cite.label: Build and manage flows with Flow Designer

sections.h: Callback is not a Calling call-queue night service
paragraphs: Webex Calling call queues have their own night service and forced forwarding. Those are Calling features.
A contact center callback is the Flow Designer activity. Configure it there.

cite.label: Configure a Webex Calling call queue

quiz.why: Later nodes do not see the contact.

choices: The same object as Calling night service
Does not place a real PSTN call

quiz.q: Screen pop after a blind transfer
choices: Does not run for that contact

cards.back: A Calling call-queue feature, not this.

steps.expect: Destination type, not a secret number

lessons.title: What the agent sees
lessons.summary: The desktop profile and the screen pop decide the agent's view. States and timers that are not in the article are not in this lesson.
objectives: Place Screen Pop before the offer
Match the desktop profile to the job
Leave undocumented timers out

diagram.caption: Offer the contact with the data you already fetched.

steps.label: Set the screen pop from variables
steps.detail: Account data from HTTP, the menu choice, and the queue name are typical fields.

steps.label: Premium or Standard
steps.detail: The desktop profile is what lets them use the tools. A supervisor profile is not an agent profile.

steps.label: Strategy offers the contact
steps.detail: LAA or BAA, or Queue To Agent. The agent must be on the team and allowed to take the channel.

steps.label: Look up RONA if you need a number
steps.detail: This lab will not print one. If your design depends on a timer, paste the sentence from the current article.

paragraphs: The Flow Designer article describes event flows beside the main flow. They handle events rather than the happy path from Start Flow.
This lab's canvas is the main path. When you need an event flow, build it in Cisco's designer and cite the event you handled.

paragraphs: Quality management, workforce management, and analytics are the workforce optimization suite, not buttons this lesson invents on the desktop.
The next track covers that suite and the AI agent activities.

choices: Are separate from the main Start Flow path
Are the same canvas with no difference

It does not prove Cisco will route a live contact, license an agent, or accept the JSON.
